nodes.content: Develop reinforcement learning transfer for robotic manipulation that reuses skills under hidden dynamics shifts while limiting negative transfer.
requirements: Match from-scratch success rates using 50% fewer target interactions when manipulation dynamics partially overlap.
On incompatible targets, stay within 5 percentage points of from-scratch success under equal interaction budgets.

nodes.content: Use five-step dynamics probes and confidence-gated source skills alongside a scratch policy, disabling reuse when normalized prediction error exceeds 0.2.
Probe-gated transfer matches scratch success at half the interactions on overlapping dynamics; incompatible-target success stays within 5 points of scratch.
On ShiftManip-12, compare gated transfer at 10k interactions against scratch at 20k (overlapping dynamics) or 10k (incompatible dynamics).
ShiftManip-12 success: overlapping gated 78%/10k versus scratch 77%/20k; incompatible gated 61% versus scratch 63%, both 10k.
Do five-step dynamics probes flag incompatible contact transitions at the 0.2 error cutoff before skill reuse harms success?
Using ShiftManip-12's 61%-versus-63% incompatible baseline, audit five-step probes' pre-reuse detection recall and success loss at error cutoffs 0.1/0.2/0.3.
Run ShiftManip-12 incompatible-target trials at error cutoffs 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3; measure pre-reuse detection recall and 10k-interaction success.
ShiftManip-12 audit.csv records cutoffs 0.1/0.2/0.3, pre-reuse detection recall of 94/87/71%, and 10k success of 60/61/56%, respectively.
Validate audit.csv against trial logs; compute missed-transition rates and success deficits versus 63% scratch, with bootstrap intervals by cutoff.
Validated logs: 0.2 cutoff missed 13% of incompatible transitions and trailed scratch by 2 points; 0.3 missed 29%, trailing 7.
Ablate probing and confidence gating on ShiftManip-12 across five seeds; compare 10k success and transferred-skill usage with full gating.
Five-seed ablation on ShiftManip-12's incompatible compliant-gripper target: full gating reached 47% success versus scratch 55% and ungated transfer 52%.
Are false-positive incompatibility flags or five-step probe costs responsible for the compliant-gripper target’s eight-point deficit versus scratch?
Using validated cutoff logs and compliant-gripper trials, compare oracle versus learned flags and free versus charged probes at 10k interactions.
Run a compliant-gripper ablation crossing oracle versus learned incompatibility flags with charged versus free five-step probes; measure 10k-interaction success.
CompliantGrip-ablation.csv records 10k success: learned/charged 47%, learned/free 49%, oracle/charged 53%, oracle/free 55%; scratch 55%.
Replace fixed cutoff with tactile-conditioned compatibility gating and scratch fallback; probe only when expected transfer gains exceed interaction costs.
Tactile-conditioned gating recovers ≥4 compliant-gripper success points by reducing false-positive flags; eliminating probe costs alone recovers ≤2.
Using CompliantGrip-ablation.csv baselines, compare tactile-adaptive versus fixed gating across five ShiftManip-12 seeds; measure false flags, probe costs, and success.
Five-seed ShiftManip-12: tactile gating cut compliant-gripper false flags 31%→12% and raised success 47%→53%; free probes alone gained 2 points.
Using CompliantGrip-ablation.csv baselines, mask tactile inputs in compliant-gripper gating with probe budgets fixed; compare false flags and 10k success.
With tactile inputs masked and probe budgets fixed, compliant-gripper success remained 53%, with 13% false flags versus 12% unmasked.
Does adaptive calibration, rather than tactile sensing, explain the six-point compliant-gripper success gain under fixed probe budgets?
Using the 47%-to-53% gain and tactile-masked 53% baseline, compare adaptive versus fixed calibration at matched probe budgets across five seeds.
Using 53% masked/unmasked baselines, cross adaptive/fixed calibration and tactile presence at matched probe budgets; measure success and false flags.
Matched-budget compliant-gripper success was 53% with adaptive calibration versus 47% fixed, regardless of tactile inputs, refuting tactile causality.
Adaptive error-quantile calibration, not tactile sensing, should keep incompatible-target false flags below 15% and success within five scratch points.
Given matched-budget calibration gains, test error-quantile gating across six incompatible ShiftManip-12 targets; measure false flags and 10k success versus scratch.
Across six incompatible ShiftManip-12 targets, calibrated gating held false flags at 9–14% and 10k success within four points of scratch.
Adopt tactile-free error-quantile gating: calibration drives the 47%→53% gain, and six incompatible targets remain within four scratch points.
Warm-start from the source skill whose bootstrapped target-return lower bound exceeds scratch; otherwise train from scratch.
At fixed probe budgets, return-bound gating should cut compliant-gripper false flags below 15% and raise success from 47% to ≥52%.
Run five-seed ShiftManip-12 return-bound gating trials at matched probe budgets; measure compliant-gripper false flags and 10k success versus scratch.
Five-seed compliant-gripper trials: return-bound gating cut false flags from 31% to 11% and raised 10k success from 47% to 54%.
Test return-bound gating on held-out ShiftManip-12 targets: overlapping at 10k versus scratch at 20k; incompatible at 10k versus scratch.
Held-out overlapping targets: return-bound gating reached 66% success at 10k interactions versus scratch 76% at 20k, missing transfer-efficiency target.
Does return-bound gating reject useful source skills on held-out overlapping targets because early target-return estimates are too conservative?
Using 54% compliant-gripper and 66%-versus-76% overlap results, compare rejected skills’ oracle returns against 80/95/99% bootstrap bounds.
Replay rejected skills at 80/95/99% bootstrap bounds; log oracle returns and 10k overlap/gripper success against 66%/54% baselines.
At 95% bounds, 42% of rejected overlapping skills outperformed scratch in oracle replay; 80% bounds raised success 66%→75%.
Reject fixed 95% return bounds: gripper protection costs overlapping-target success; prioritize testing 80% bounds for incompatible-target safety.
Combine 80% return-bound skill selection with an error-quantile incompatibility veto and scratch fallback to preserve reuse without unsafe transfer.
Hybrid gating reaches scratch’s 20k success with 10k interactions on overlapping targets and stays within five points on incompatible targets.
On held-out ShiftManip-12 targets, compare hybrid 10k success against scratch at 20k overlapping and 10k incompatible interactions across five seeds.
Five-seed held-out ShiftManip-12: hybrid success was 77%/10k versus scratch 76%/20k overlapping; 60% versus 63% incompatible at 10k.
Using ShiftManip-12 baselines, test hybrid gating on 24 unseen shifts across 10 seeds; check 10k/20k parity and ≤5-point incompatibility deficits.
Run 10-seed HybridManip-24 with randomized friction, payload, gripper compliance, and actuator lag; record per-shift success at 10k/20k.
HybridManip-24 results.csv records per-shift, 10-seed success for hybrid and scratch, interaction budgets, dynamics labels, and incompatibility-veto decisions.
Validate HybridManip-24 results.csv budgets and seeds; bootstrap hybrid-10k versus scratch-20k overlap parity and equal-budget incompatible deficits per shift.
Validated HybridManip-24: 12 overlapping shifts averaged 76% hybrid/10k versus 75% scratch/20k; 12 incompatible shifts had ≤4-point equal-budget deficits.
Adopt hybrid gating: held-out and HybridManip-24 tests matched 20k scratch success at 10k overlap interactions, with ≤4-point incompatible deficits.
